finding.title: Add semantics/tooltip to the icon-only close and back buttons in step_starting_position.dart and track_management_body.dart
finding.why: Both IconButtons carry no `tooltip` (nor an explicit Semantics label), unlike every other icon-only button in this batch (scope_tiles.dart, scope_views.dart, curriculum_picker_step.dart all set tooltip). A screen-reader user hits an unlabeled 'button' for the selection-clear action and for the track-management screen's primary back action.
finding.recommendation: Add tooltip: l10n.<key> to both, mirroring the pattern already used for the other IconButtons in the same files.
acceptance_criteria: Both IconButtons have a non-null, localized tooltip.
A semantics test (find.bySemanticsLabel or similar) locates each button by its new label.

finding.title: Wrap saveOrder/resetToDefault's reorder-amnesty stamp in the same transaction as the order write
finding.rule: DB-2 (>1 write = one transaction()) + Nygard partial-failure lens
finding.why: _stampReorderAt does its own read+write OUTSIDE the transaction that persists the order change, in both saveOrder and resetToDefault. A process death or DB error between the two calls leaves the new order committed but the overdue-amnesty stamp missing (or the delete committed but the stamp missing on resetToDefault) — the code's own comment about wrapping upserts 'so a mid-loop crash cannot leave a half-shuffled state' shows the author cared about exactly this class of bug but didn't extend it to the second write.
finding.recommendation: Move the _stampReorderAt call inside the same _database.transaction(...) block in both saveOrder and resetToDefault.
acceptance_criteria: Test: throw inside a fake trackDao.stampReorderAt call and assert the learning_order upsert rows are also rolled back as one atomic unit

finding.title: Inject FakeLocalDayClock into TrackCreationService's B3 back-date tests instead of reading the wall clock

evidence.quote: expect(daysBack, 5, reason: 'offset:5 must be exactly 5 days in the past');

finding.why: Neither B3 test overrides LocalDayClock, so DateTimeFactory.nowUtc() reads the real system clock both for the test's 'before' and again inside the SUT's _parseProgramStartingRef moments later. Duration.inDays truncates: (Duration(days:5) - Duration(microseconds:1)).inDays == 4, verified directly in this Dart VM; an empirical 200k-iteration back-to-back DateTime.now() sample in this same environment showed roughly 4% of pairs returning a non-zero gap (up to 70us), meaning daysBack can legitimately compute to 4 instead of 5 and fail expect(daysBack, 5, ...) for reasons unrelated to any real regression. This is exactly the flakiness class LocalDayClock/FakeLocalDayClock exists to eliminate, and the sibling provision_track_use_case_test.dart correctly uses FakeLocalDayClock for the equivalent B3 assertions — this file is the outlier.
finding.recommendation: Thread a FakeLocalDayClock(seed) into TrackCreationService/_parseProgramStartingRef so the test's 'before' and the SUT's 'now' are the identical fixed instant, making daysBack deterministic.
acceptance_criteria: Test passes across many repeated runs with an artificial delay inserted between test setup and SUT invocation
Test no longer depends on two independent real-clock reads landing in the same tick

finding.title: Fix the vacuous ChazaraInlineSetup custom-round tests in edit_track_screen_l1_test.dart
finding.rule: TQ-8 (tautological tests / assertions weaker than what the source can do wrong)
finding.why: The file's own header claims coverage of 'Custom cycle enforces min 1 / max 5 rounds', and the real production logic exists (step_chazara.dart:295 onRemove null guard, :302-303 'if (_customDelays.length < 5) AddRoundChip'), but all 3 tests against it are vacuous: two probe icon constants (Icons.add_circle_outline_rounded, Icons.add_rounded) that AddRoundChip never renders — it renders Icons.add, confirmed by reading chazara_widgets.dart:196 — so their assertions pass independent of real widget behavior, and the third asserts List.length >= 0, a Dart-level tautology that is always true. A future change that broke min/max-round enforcement entirely (always 6+ rounds allowed, or the last round removable) would leave this whole test group green.
finding.recommendation: Fix the icon finders to Icons.add scoped via a Key/byWidgetPredicate (to avoid ambiguity with the unrelated TinyCircleButton Icons.add elsewhere), fix initialDelays: [1] to [3] in the add-round test per its own comment so it actually starts in custom mode, and replace the tautological length check with a real assertion on round count / IconButton.onPressed before vs after.
acceptance_criteria: Deliberately make _customDelays.length < 5 unconditionally true and confirm the 'hidden at 5' test now fails
Deliberately make onRemove always non-null and confirm the 'remove absent at 1' test now fails

finding.title: Re-point add_track_smart_label_test.dart at the code path that actually produces the track-created toast label
finding.rule: TQ-8 (stale regression test no longer covers the bug it claims to guard)
finding.why: The test's docstring says smartTrackLabelForScope is a 'Pure helper extracted from AddTrackFlow._getSmartDefault', and defines a local copy that calls CurriculumLabels.transliterateNamedValue directly. But the real, current _getSmartDefault (add_track_flow_screen.dart:670-684) was refactored (comment: 'F-05/F-21/run7: always use the curriculum label for the track's default name... not the last-selected seder') and now calls curriculumLabelText exclusively — it contains no reference to transliterateNamedValue at all. The test still passes because transliterateNamedValue is real and still used elsewhere (curriculum_label.dart), but it no longer exercises the actual toast-label path it was written to regression-guard (R1: English 'Genesis' leaking into the Hebrew-mode toast). A future regression in curriculumLabelText's Hebrew-terms/transliteration-variant wiring — the mechanism that actually produces the toast text today — would ship with this suite fully green.
finding.recommendation: Either delete the private-method fiction and retarget this file at curriculumLabelText's transliteration-variant behavior directly, or extract _getSmartDefault's label logic to a public, directly-testable function and call the real thing from the test.
acceptance_criteria: Test imports and calls the real function on the _getSmartDefault code path, not a hand-copied reimplementation
Deliberately breaking curriculumLabelText's Hebrew-terms wiring causes this test to fail
